questions.question_text:
A positive integer has exactly six distinct factors.
How is it classified?

options.why: Ignored that prime numbers have exactly two distinct factors, not six.
Used the special classification for $0$ and $1$ despite the number having six factors.

questions.solution_text: Six factors is more than two, so the number is composite.

questions.question_text:
A student claims $121$ is prime because it is odd.
Which correction is valid?

options.text: $121$ is prime because every odd number is prime.
options.why: Used oddness alone as proof and ignored possible odd factor pairs.

options.text: $121$ is neither because its digits repeat.
options.why: Used repeated digits, which do not determine prime or composite classification.

options.text: $121$ is composite because it is greater than $100$.
options.why: Used size alone instead of showing a factor other than $1$ and $121$.

questions.solution_text:
$11 \times 11=121$
So $121$ has more than two factors and is composite.

questions.question_text: Which number below is a composite number?

options.why: It has only one positive factor, so it is neither prime nor composite.
It has exactly two positive factors, so it is a prime number.
Its only positive factors are 1 and 7, so it is prime.

questions.solution_text: 6 has more than two positive factors: 1, 2, 3, and 6. Therefore, 6 is composite.
